newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KPC discusses refinery partnership with SINOPEC.
newsitem.headline: KPC discusses refinery partnership with SINOPEC.

text.p: Kuwait's Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi on Monday discussed long-term crude supplies and refinery partnership prospects with China Petrochemical Corp (SINOPEC).

The two sides "discussed Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) joining SINOPEC in a project to own and modernise an existing refinery in China and supply it with Kuwaiti crude," a KPC statement said without naming the refinery.
Mazeedi is also chairman of the state-owned KPC which runs Kuwait's oil sector, including domestic and overseas refining.

Kuwait, which has a refining and downstream network in Europe, has a local refining capacity of about 895,000 barrels per day (bpd). It is currently finalising refinery projects in the Indian sub-continent and studying further prospects in Asia.
The statement said KPC's strategy of finding new long-term markets for Kuwaiti crudes includes "investing in this important market through owning refineries and marketing in China."
The two sides agreed to hold further discussions after KPC studies detailed information supplied by China's giant SINOPEC.
Kuwait, which controls 10 percent of the world's proven oil reserves, produces about two million bpd of crude oil.
